info.description: HTTP API for managing Machinarchy environments, SSH hosts, and operations.
info.title: Machinarchy API

post.description: Authenticates an account, returns a JWT, and sets the auth_token cookie.
Revokes the session of the token sent (cookie or bearer) and clears the cookie. Succeeds even without a valid session.
Creates an account, returns a JWT, and sets the auth_token cookie.

get.summary: Get the controller public key agents must trust

get.description: Owner only. Secrets are never returned.

post.description:
Owner only. The secret is returned once and stored only as a hash. It enrols one agent before it expires
(default 1 hour), optionally only from the given hostname. Configure it on the host as
MACHINARCHY_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN_FILE.
post.summary: Issue a single-use agent enrolment token

delete.summary: Revoke an unused agent enrolment token

post.description:
200 means the agent answered. The body is the agent's signed result: check its `status`.
`succeeded` carries `output`. `rejected` (with `code`, for example `capability_unavailable`)
and `failed` are the agent's own answers and also return 200.
HTTP errors mean there was no answer: 503 when this process runs no gateway or the agent has no live lease,
504 when the agent did not answer within `timeoutSeconds` (default 15, at most 20).
post.summary: Run a capability on an agent and wait for its result

get.description: Requires a human workspace owner session; API tokens are refused. Events are append-only and never contain credentials. Page backwards by passing the smallest id received as before_id.

parameters.description: Only events with this action, for example member.role_changed
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: Only events with a smaller id (paging cursor)
parameters.name: before_id

get.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. Recomputes every event's hash and link. A valid result proves no earlier event was edited, removed, or reordered; it cannot detect events removed from the end, so record headHash somewhere outside the database to detect that.
Returns SecretRefs only, never secret values.

get.summary: Get an Access Profile with its current spec

put.summary: Create a new Access Profile revision

delete.description: Owner only; refused with 409 while a host is bound to it.

get.description: Keyset-paginated; filter by selector, environment ID and phase.

post.description: Binding an Access Profile needs the workspace owner.

put.description: Changing the profile, endpoint or trust of a bound host needs the owner.

delete.description: Refused with 409 while an operation targets the host.

post.description:
Workspace owner only. Name the exact fingerprints you reviewed (usually status.observedHostKeys) and the
spec generation you saw. A Host that already trusts keys needs replace=true, so a changed key is never
accepted by accident. The Host is then verified again with the trusted keys.
post.summary: Trust a host's SSH host keys

get.description: Newest first; summaries never contain argv or output.

post.description: Target hostIds, or a rule; expectTargetsHash binds the run to a preview (409 targets_changed).

post.summary: Preview the hosts a target rule selects

get.description: Readers see no argv or output.

One stream of one target's output: live while a detached command runs (poll it to follow), final afterwards. Long output keeps its first and last 15 KiB; bytes is the full size. Only callers allowed to execute runs may read output.

parameters.description: Stream byte offset to start from (the previous response's next)
parameters.name: from

post.description: Checks the current password, stores the new one (12–72 bytes) and revokes every login session of the caller, including this one: log in again. API tokens are not affected.

get.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. API tokens are refused.

put.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. Takes effect on the member's next request, including for API tokens, whose effective role never exceeds the membership role. A workspace must always keep at least one owner. The change is recorded in the structured server log.

post.summary: Copy an earlier revision into a new one
Create a secret from a write-only value
Rewrap stored keys under the active KEK

get.description: The caller's active login sessions, newest first; "current" marks the one used for this request. Needs a login session (API tokens are refused).

delete.description: Revokes every login session of the caller, including the current one. API tokens are not affected.

get.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. Returns metadata for tokens created by the current user; plaintext secrets are never returned.

post.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. Tokens are limited to operator or reader and their effective access cannot exceed the owner's current workspace membership role. Plaintext is returned only in this response.

delete.description: Requires a human workspace owner session. The revoked token is rejected on its next request.

nextPublicKey.description: NextPublicKey is announced for a rotation; empty otherwise.

publicKeys.description: PublicKeys is the value for MACHINARCHY_AGENT_CONTROLLER_PUBLIC_KEY.

hostname.description: Hostname, when set, is the only hostname this token enrols.

token.description: Token is the secret, shown only in this response.

headHash.description:
HeadHash is the hash of the newest event. Record it somewhere outside the
database (a ticket, a log line) to detect later truncation of the tail.

current.description: Current marks the session the request was made with.

fingerprints.description:
Fingerprints are the exact SHA256:… fingerprints to trust, normally the
Host's status.observedHostKeys as reviewed.

generation.description: Generation is the Host spec generation the caller reviewed.

replace.description: Replace must be set to change keys the Host already trusts.

execution.description: Execution configures detached runs on the profile's hosts.

hostKeyPolicy.description:
HostKeyPolicy and HostCertificateAuthorities decide how the hosts that
use this profile become trusted (see hostkeys.go).

maxOutputFileBytes.description:
MaxOutputFileBytes caps each output file on the host (ulimit -f);
0 means 100 MiB.

stateRoot.description:
StateRoot holds per-target directories on the host; the default is
$HOME/.local/state/machinarchy of the login user.

supervisor.description:
Supervisor: auto (default; systemd-run when usable, else setsid),
systemd, setsid, or attached (detached runs are refused).

accessTarget.description:
AccessTarget is host-owned connector-neutral location and trust material.
Its interpretation is restricted to the selected connector adapter.

observedHostKeys.description:
ObservedHostKeys are the SSH host keys last seen on the network, kept
so an owner can approve them (or see what changed).

targetsHash.description:
TargetsHash identifies the exact Host IDs and generations matched, so a
submission can require that it runs on what was reviewed.

attempt.description:
Attempt counts launches of this target (1 for the first). A launch
proven never to have started is retried up to MaxLaunchAttempts.

deadline.description:
Deadline is when the command must have finished: launch time plus
the run's timeout, or the Operation deadline if earlier.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the Host endpoint at launch; a poll of a moved Host is
treated as unreachable rather than sent to another machine.

mode.description:
Mode is systemd or setsid; empty means the launch reply never arrived
(the connection failed mid-launch), so the poller must find out
whether the command started.

root.description: Root is the state root used at launch ("" = the default).

lastSeenAt.description:
LastSeenAt is when a scan last saw the key. The reconciler reuses a
recent scan instead of connecting again (see HostReconciler).

launch.description:
Launch and Live are set for detached runs: how to reach the command,
and its captured output (kept after it ends, so output can be read by
byte offset). Live is stored encrypted on its own and never serialized
with the target; the output endpoint serves it to callers allowed to
see output.

progress.description: Progress summarizes Live for API readers: sizes and timing, no output.

detach.description:
Detach runs the command under a supervisor on each host and ends the
SSH session right after the launch (AUDIT/10b §1). The timeout may
then be up to MaxDetachedTimeoutSeconds; attached runs keep
MaxAttachedTimeoutSeconds.

bytes.description: Bytes is the stream's full size; Truncated means part of it is gone.

from.description:
From and Next are stream byte offsets: Text covers the stream from
From on, and the next request should ask for Next. A detached target
keeps its first and last 15 KiB; a part of the stream that was not
kept appears in Text as one "[… N bytes omitted …]" line.

live.description:
Live is true until the target is final (pending or running): more
output can follow, so a follower keeps asking.

BearerAuth.description: Supply a JWT as `Bearer <token>`. The API also accepts the auth_token cookie.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
